entries.title: Proverbs 15:1
segments: Mild and conciliatory words often win those whom harsh and irritating language would only have driven farther from us.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:4
segments:
A breach in the spirit; inflicting upon it grievous wounds. 
 
A ungoverned tongue is the source of misery and ruin to its possessor and to others.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:6
segments: The blessing of God makes the possessions of the righteous man, be they great or small, a source of comfort and usefulness to him; but a wicked man's troubles increase with his riches.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:7
segments: "Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh," whether it be wisdom or folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:8
segments: The sacrifice of the wicked; the sacrifice which he offers to God, put here for all his religious services.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:10
segments:
The way; the way of uprightness. 
 
All presumptous transgressors hate reproof, and for this reason they are in imminent danger of persisting in sin till it ends in their destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:11
segments: Hell and destruction; the invisible world.
We may flatter and deceive our fellow sinners, but with God hypocrisy and dissimulation can have no place.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:12
segments: Since scorners are unwilling to receive correction from the wise, they must remain fools, and the companions of fools.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:13
segments: Cheerfulness is both the privilege and duty of every Christian; it contributes alike to his own comfort and usefulness, and to the welfare of those around him.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:15
segments:
The afflicted; the man who, under the pressure of outward trouble, yields to despondency and gloom. 
 
  Merry; cheerful and contented. 
 
Since affliction is the lot of all men, we should place our happiness rather in a contented and believing spirit, than in the possession of outward good.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:16
segments: Great treasure; the reference is to the treasures of the wicked.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:17
segments: Stalled ox; fatted in the stall.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:18
segments: He who would "live peaceably with all men," must first learn to govern his own spirit.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:19
segments:
As a hedge of thorns; he meets with perpetual difficulty and trouble. 
 
  Made plain; it is a highway on which he can walk without impediment. 
 
God has so ordered the course of things in this world, that the industrious alone can enjoy life: the slothful meet with difficulties and troubles on every side.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:20
segments: Despiseth his mother; and thus fills her heart with heaviness.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:22
segments: The beginning of success is deliberation and wise counsels.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:23
segments: In the timely and right use of speech lies an important part of our influence and usefulness.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:24
segments: Is above; leads upward to God and blessedness.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:25
segments: God's almighty power is as terrible to the proud oppressor and his house, as it is glorious to the poor and defenceless who put their trust in him.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:26
segments: Pleasant; acceptable to God and men.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:27
segments:
Gifts; bribes given to pervert justice. 
 
Unrighteous gain brings trouble and misery to its owner and his family.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:30
segments: The light of the eyes; either what is bright and pleasant to behold, or a friendly look.
A good report; good tidings.

entries.title: Proverbs 15:33
segments: Is the instruction of wisdom; it guides men into the possession of wisdom.
